about: Definitions only. Measured values live in each run's tpm.json; baselines live in tpm_baseline.json. threshold_status: TBD (no limit yet), TBR (proposed limit, shown with margin, never pass or fail), Confirmed (a limit that fails a run when breached). A threshold is in the TPM's unit, or {factor, of} for a limit relative to a run fact (exposure_seconds, frame_interval_seconds). cold_only: true marks a limit that applies only to a --cold run (the file cache was dropped before it); a warm run still measures the value but gets no limit for it.

tpms.name: time_to_app_ready
tpms.title: Time until the app is ready
tpms.why: You start the app and want to use it before you lose your train of thought.
tpms.source: Nielsen response-time limits (0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the flow of thought, 10 s is the attention limit); 5 s threshold, 2 s objective is reachable on this CPU (measured about 1.8 s).

tpms.name: time_to_app_ready_cold
tpms.title: Time until the app is ready, cold start
tpms.why: The first start after a reboot reads everything from the disk, and you still want to begin without losing your train of thought.
tpms.method: performance mark in the page, first load of the run; the limit applies only to a --cold run (files dropped from the page cache before the run)
tpms.source: proposal 2026-11-06

tpms.name: first_display_open[{display}]
tpms.title: First open of a display, cold start
tpms.why: The first time you open a display after a cold start, the click should still answer quickly.
tpms.method: click-to-settled time of the first visit to each display in lap 1 of the flow; the limit applies only to a --cold run
tpms.source: proposal 2026-11-06

tpms.name: first_rpc[{rpc}]
tpms.title: First backend call, cold start
tpms.why: The first query on real data reads database pages that are not in memory yet.
tpms.method: latency of the first call of each method in the run (the page's own timing of the fetch); the limit applies only to a --cold run
tpms.source: proposal 2026-11-06

tpms.name: display_switch_median
tpms.title: Display switch, typical
tpms.why: Switching displays should feel immediate.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: display_switch_p95
tpms.title: Display switch, slow cases
tpms.why: Even the slow switches must keep your flow of thought.
tpms.source: Nielsen response-time limits (0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the flow of thought, 10 s is the attention limit).

confirmed.source: Nielsen response-time limits (0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps the flow of thought, 10 s is the attention limit).

tpms.name: display_switch_median[{display}]
tpms.title: Display switch per display
tpms.why: A single slow display shows up here.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: interaction_latency_select_target
tpms.title: Select a target (response time)
tpms.why: A click should show its result before you doubt that it worked.
tpms.source: Google Core Web Vitals Interaction to Next Paint: good up to 200 ms, poor over 500 ms.

confirmed.source: Google Core Web Vitals Interaction to Next Paint: good up to 200 ms, poor over 500 ms.

tpms.name: interaction_latency_open_night
tpms.title: Open an observing night (response time)
tpms.why: A click should show its result before you doubt that it worked.
tpms.source: Between the 1 s flow limit and the 10 s attention limit (Nielsen); the night review loads much data.

tpms.name: interaction_latency_change_tab
tpms.title: Change a tab (response time)
tpms.why: A click should show its result before you doubt that it worked.
tpms.source: No limit set yet.

tpms.name: total_blocking_time[Load app]
tpms.title: Main-thread blocking at load
tpms.why: A blocked page cannot answer clicks.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: total_blocking_time[{display}]
tpms.title: Main-thread blocking per display
tpms.why: A blocked page cannot answer clicks.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: inp_worst
tpms.title: Worst Interaction to Next Paint
tpms.why: No click should ever feel stuck.
tpms.source: Google Core Web Vitals: good up to 200 ms, poor over 500 ms.

confirmed.source: Google Core Web Vitals: good up to 200 ms, poor over 500 ms.

tpms.source: Google Core Web Vitals: good up to 0.1, poor over 0.25.

confirmed.source: Google Core Web Vitals: good up to 0.1, poor over 0.25.

tpms.title: JavaScript size at load

tpms.name: request_count_load
tpms.title: Requests at load
tpms.why: Fewer requests mean a faster start.

tpms.name: planetarium_fps_panning
tpms.title: Planetarium frame rate while panning
tpms.why: The sky should follow your hand smoothly.
tpms.source: 60 Hz laptop panel caps the rate at 60 fps; below 30 fps the motion looks choppy.

confirmed.source: 60 Hz laptop panel caps the rate at 60 fps; below 30 fps the motion looks choppy.

tpms.name: planetarium_fps_zooming
tpms.title: Planetarium frame rate while the zoom animates
tpms.why: The sky should zoom smoothly. The sky map draws only while it moves, so only the frames of the animation count.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: drawn frames per second inside stretches of active animation (idle gaps of 100 ms or more excluded)
tpms.source: 60 Hz laptop panel caps the rate at 60 fps; below 30 fps the motion looks choppy.

confirmed.source: 60 Hz laptop panel caps the rate at 60 fps; below 30 fps the motion looks choppy.

tpms.name: fps_hw
tpms.title: Planetarium frame rate on real graphics
tpms.why: The same rate, kept only when WebGL drew on a graphics card.
tpms.source: 60 Hz laptop panel caps the rate at 60 fps; below 30 fps the motion looks choppy.

confirmed.source: 60 Hz laptop panel caps the rate at 60 fps; below 30 fps the motion looks choppy.

tpms.name: pan_frame_ms_p50
tpms.title: Pan frame time, typical
tpms.why: Frame time shows how much of a frame the page uses.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium pan
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: pan_frame_ms_p95
tpms.title: Pan frame time, slow frames
tpms.why: A few slow frames are the stutter you see.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium pan
tpms.source: Derived from the frame-rate limits: 1000/30 = 33.3 ms and 1000/60 = 16.7 ms.

confirmed.source: Derived from the frame-rate limits: 1000/30 = 33.3 ms and 1000/60 = 16.7 ms.

tpms.name: star_project_ms_p50
tpms.title: Star projection and upload time
tpms.why: Shows where a slow frame spends its time.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: overlay_draw_ms_p50
tpms.title: Overlay drawing time
tpms.why: Shows where a slow frame spends its time.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: gpu_ms_p50
tpms.title: Graphics process busy time per frame
tpms.why: Shows whether the graphics card or the page limits the frame rate.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium pan
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_frame_ms_p50
tpms.title: Zoom frame time while animating, typical
tpms.why: Frame time shows how much of a frame the page uses while the zoom eases (idle gaps between wheel ticks are left out).
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: frames of active animation only (a gap of 100 ms or more is the sky map idle, not a slow frame)
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_frame_ms_p95
tpms.title: Zoom frame time while animating, slow frames
tpms.why: A few slow frames are the stutter you see while the zoom eases. Idle gaps between wheel ticks are not frames: the sky map draws only when something changes.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: frames of active animation only (a gap of 100 ms or more is the sky map idle, not a slow frame)
tpms.source: Derived from the frame-rate limits: 1000/30 = 33.3 ms and 1000/60 = 16.7 ms.

confirmed.source: Derived from the frame-rate limits: 1000/30 = 33.3 ms and 1000/60 = 16.7 ms.

tpms.name: zoom_slow_frames
tpms.title: Zoom frames over 20 ms
tpms.why: Each one is a frame that missed a 60 Hz screen's refresh (took over 1.2 refreshes) while the zoom was animating.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: count of intervals over 20 ms (1.2 refreshes of a 60 Hz screen) inside active animation
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_tick_latency_ms_p50
tpms.title: Zoom response to a wheel tick, typical
tpms.why: How long after you turn the wheel the sky first changes.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: from the wheel input event to the first frame drawn after it, per tick
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_tick_latency_ms_p95
tpms.title: Zoom response to a wheel tick, slow
tpms.why: The slowest ticks are the ones that feel laggy.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: from the wheel input event to the first frame drawn after it, per tick
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_settle_ms_p50
tpms.title: Zoom settle time, typical
tpms.why: How long the zoom keeps easing after a wheel tick before the sky is still.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: from the wheel tick to the last frame of its easing (ticks whose easing runs into the next tick are left out)
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_settle_ms_p95
tpms.title: Zoom settle time, slow
tpms.why: A slow settle feels like the sky drifting after you stop.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: from the wheel tick to the last frame of its easing (ticks whose easing runs into the next tick are left out)
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_long_tasks
tpms.title: Zoom main-thread tasks over 50 ms
tpms.why: A task over 50 ms blocks the page, so the sky and the buttons cannot answer.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom: main-thread tasks longer than 50 ms in the zoom window
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_main_thread_ms_per_frame
tpms.title: Zoom main-thread time per frame
tpms.why: Shows whether the page's own code limits the frame rate.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: zoom_gpu_ms_p50
tpms.title: Zoom graphics busy time per frame
tpms.why: Shows whether the graphics card limits the frame rate.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of the Planetarium zoom
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: planetarium_idle_draws_per_second
tpms.title: Planetarium draws while idle
tpms.why: A still sky should cost nothing: no drawn frame, no battery, no fan.
tpms.method: DevTools trace of a 3 s idle window after the zoom has settled: drawn compositor frames divided by the window length. Expected about 0 after the idle fix.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Expectation about 0 draws per second after the idle fix; needs a measured run before a limit is proposed.

tpms.name: js_heap_after_last_lap
tpms.title: JavaScript memory after the last lap
tpms.why: Memory use of the page.
tpms.method: DevTools heap size after garbage collection
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: js_heap_growth_per_lap
tpms.title: JavaScript memory growth per lap
tpms.why: A night of use must not leak memory.
tpms.method: DevTools heap size after garbage collection
tpms.source: A 10 h night is about 1000 display visits; growth must stay near zero.

tpms.name: electron_{process}_peak_memory_mb
tpms.title: Electron process peak memory
tpms.why: Memory the desktop shell uses.

tpms.name: electron_{process}_mean_cpu_percent

tpms.name: backend_idle_cpu_percent

tpms.why: The backend runs all night, on battery in the field.

tpms.name: frames_auto_downloaded
tpms.title: Frames copied into the library by the app
tpms.why: The app should bring in every frame the camera takes.
tpms.source: No limit set yet. Needs a baseline run and a user need first.

tpms.name: guide_events_received
tpms.title: Guide steps received from PHD2
tpms.why: The app should see every guide step.

tpms.name: frame_to_library_seconds
tpms.title: Time from a new frame to its copy in the library

tpms.name: guide_log_lines_pulled

tpms.name: console_errors
tpms.title: Browser console errors
tpms.why: The user should see no errors in the web browser console.
tpms.method: Console messages of level error and uncaught page errors during the whole flow (Chrome flow and Electron renderer, including the Electron start-up and idle time). Each message and its source URL goes to info.errors.
tpms.source: User requirement 2026-11-06: no errors in the browser console and no error notifications at start-up; the limit is zero.

confirmed.source: I should be getting no errors in the web browser console, and no error notifications at start-up.

tpms.name: failed_requests
tpms.title: Failed requests
tpms.why: A request that fails (status 400 or more, or no answer) is a broken image, call or file.
tpms.method: Responses with status 400 or more and failed requests during the whole flow, except requests the browser cancelled (net::ERR_ABORTED, listed apart). Each URL and status goes to info.errors.
tpms.source: User requirement 2026-11-06: no errors in the browser console and no error notifications at start-up; the limit is zero.

confirmed.source: I should be getting no errors in the web browser console, and no error notifications at start-up.

tpms.name: error_toasts
tpms.title: Error and warning toasts
tpms.why: The user should see no error or warning pop-ups from a clean run.
tpms.method: In-app toasts of kind error or warning, caught from the window event astrometrics:toast that emitToast sends. Each text goes to info.errors.
tpms.source: User requirement 2026-11-06: no errors in the browser console and no error notifications at start-up; the limit is zero.

confirmed.source: I should be getting no errors in the web browser console, and no error notifications at start-up.

tpms.name: desktop_notifications
tpms.title: Desktop notifications
tpms.why: The app must send no native notification, and none at start-up.
tpms.method: Native notifications the page asked Electron to show (the show-notification IPC channel, counted in electron/perf_metrics.js when ASTROMETRICS_PERF_METRICS is set). Only an Electron run measures it; counted before the app's own cooldown.
tpms.source: User requirement 2026-11-06: no errors in the browser console and no error notifications at start-up; the limit is zero.

confirmed.source: I should be getting no errors in the web browser console, and no error notifications at start-up.

tpms.name: backend_error_log_lines
tpms.title: Backend ERROR log lines
tpms.why: A clean run should leave no line at ERROR level in the backend log.
tpms.method: Lines at ERROR or CRITICAL level in the throwaway backend's backend.log, from the backend's start to its end. Each line goes to info.errors.
tpms.source: User requirement 2026-11-06: no errors in the browser console and no error notifications at start-up; the limit is zero.

confirmed.source: I should be getting no errors in the web browser console, and no error notifications at start-up.
